Through the Android app: hfmodels-android samples/loops on litertlm-android 0.16.1, GSM8K test question 75 (the bundled example gsm8k-75, the text and instruction of the card's GSM8K run byte for byte), thinking off, four runs on 2026-10-26 on one Galaxy S26: b1 and b2 in hold s26-h1 (12:53-13:11 JST; the eight bundled examples, the one-loop file first in b1 and the int4 file first in b2; the phone came from an 11-hour benchmark job, thermal status 3 at the hold's start), u2 in hold s26-h2 (14:03-14:12; gsm8k-75 alone, picked on the screen after 260 s of rest, thermal 0) and t1 in hold s26-h3 (14:12-14:22; the same with the screen recorder = the demo clip's run, after 330 s of rest). In all four runs the one-loop file wrote '#### 7.5' (264 chunks) and the int4 file '#### 60' = GSM8K's answer (320 chunks): the BF16 reference with one loop also writes 7.5 (the card's Loops section names question 75). The app measures walls and counts streamed chunks, not tokens: ttft_ms and the throughput fields stay null, the walls and the app's chunk rate are in metrics, with the file's place in the run (file_order_in_run) and the question's place in its pass (question_position); output_match null (the GSM8K agreement is metrics.answer_matches_gsm8k). Not entered: the other seven examples of b1 and b2 (the sample's own records, hfmodels-android samples/loops/results/2026-10-26-s26/, whose 14 answers per file order are byte for byte 2026-10-23's); the answers' dropped final mark on this runtime (a runtime hazard outside the schemas).
quantization: int4 blockwise-32 on the linear layers, codes chosen by GPTQ (Conversion notes), block scales floored at 2^-14; int8 embedding in its own section; the KV-cache writes and attention matmuls as the runtime's GPU composites (fused GPU ops; Conversion notes); no activation type declared: on the GPU it runs with the runtime's default fp16 activations
